rendered: The carbon's micropores are about ∼0.5 nm[1] across, while the electrolyte's solvent molecule is about ∼0.7 nm in diameter[2], so the pores are too small to accommodate the solvent. The sodium (metal) ion is much smaller, only about ∼0.2 nm in diameter[3]. Because the solvated ion cannot fit in the pores, the ion must desolvate at the surface of the microporous host and transport independently to the sulfur, which forms a quasi solid-state reaction at the cathode.[4][5]
